context_pointers.batching_note: Implemented at Task granularity (S0.2.1-S0.2.3 in one run) at the caller's instruction; the usual one-subtask rule was waived for schedule.

self_consistency.uv build --wheel: 0, config/aliases.yaml present in the wheel at video_agent/config/aliases.yaml
self_consistency.pre-commit run --all-files: ruff/mypy hooks passed; end-of-file-fixer rewrote two PRE-EXISTING files from earlier CDR runs (.cdr/runs/2026-08-08/002-planner/metadata.json, 003-planner/PLAN.md). Both were reverted and are NOT part of this commit.

findings_for_verifier: QC_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS is `int = Field(ge=2, le=2)`, not `Literal[2]`. Literal[int] does not coerce the string an environment variable actually delivers, so `QC_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS=2` from .env was itself rejected. The constraint is still exactly 2.

Three fields are required (no default) despite .env.example supplying a value for two of them: MAGICHOUR_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL. The plan's own test spec demands this. It means .env.example defaults and Settings defaults deliberately diverge for the two URLs; tests/unit/test_settings.py::test_required_fields_are_exactly_the_three_that_cannot_be_guessed pins the divergence and states why.

Required means PRESENT, not NON-EMPTY. MAGICHOUR_API_KEY= satisfies the field; require_magichour_api_key() raises MissingCredentialError at point of use. The app starts with the key empty, as instructed.
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is typed SecretStr although the acceptance criteria do not name it. It is half a credential pair and credential-shaped. LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY is deliberately a plain str.

AliasConfigError carries VA-GW-002 for every alias-table load failure, not only for a missing alias. gateway.md S8 defines that code for 'alias not in config'; a table that will not load resolves no alias, so it is the same condition reached earlier. No other code in observability.md S6 fits. MissingCredentialError deliberately carries NO code: inventing one would corrupt the historical registry T0.3 introduces.

The alias-only static guard bans all 16 Magic Hour model names, but 'default' (also an ordinary English word) is matched ONLY as the exact full value of a string literal, while the other 15 and every vendor name are matched in raw file text including comments. See tests/static_guards.py AMBIGUOUS_MODEL_NAMES. The consequence is that a bare `"default"` literal anywhere in src/ now fails CI.

The inline-prompt guard exempts every string that is a bare expression statement (docstrings and PEP 257 attribute docstrings), not only the first statement of a body. Without that it flagged src/video_agent/config/errors.py's own attribute docstring.

pyproject.toml gained `plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]`. Without it, mypy synthesises Settings.__init__ from the field declarations via dataclass_transform and reports every required variable as a missing argument at `Settings()`, and rejects the documented `_env_file=None`. The alternative was inline `# type: ignore[call-arg]`, which the quality bar forbids. This is not a relaxation: no ruff ignore, no per-file-ignores, no mypy overrides, no noqa were added.
pyyaml moved from the dev dependency group into project.dependencies. The alias table is parsed at startup, so it is a runtime dependency. No new package entered the lock file.

.github/workflows/ci.yml now runs `cp .env.example .env` before `make test`. The preflight validates configuration, so tests/unit/test_media_toolchain.py::test_entrypoint_exits_zero_when_the_pin_matches needs a .env in CI. Verified: the committed template alone constructs Settings successfully.

config/aliases.yaml is located by walking up from the loader module and then from the cwd. pyproject force-includes it into the wheel at video_agent/config/aliases.yaml so both a checkout and an installed wheel resolve. A Dockerfile task must still ensure the file reaches the image.

The shipped alias table declares NO canary. Sending 10% of traffic to an unproven model is a decision with a cost and is not made by leaving an example uncommented. Canary parsing and bounds are covered by fixture tests.

Prices in config/aliases.yaml are list rates transcribed when the file was written and are not reconciled against any vendor price page. The golden snapshot in tests/unit/test_alias_table.py makes a change loud, not correct.
